actual_incoming_interface_paragraphs:
In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced
modules $J(\nu)$ of
[[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the
normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the
general-field normalization/crystal clauses of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and
[[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]
(in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by
[[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the
**graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
for $\lambda,\nu\in RP_\alpha$ by
$$[J(\nu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)=[J(\nu):D(\lambda)]_q .$$
Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,\nu})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its
entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy
$a_{\nu,\nu}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd\nu$ (dominance);
equivalently $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in
$(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}(D_\nu)$.

[F1] The reduced modules $J(\nu)=F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}L(\nu)$ have
field-independent $q$-characters and well-defined classes in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha(F))$
([[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]]).

[F2] The normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ have crystal labels in $RP_\alpha$ and
their labels agree with the cellular head labels in positive characteristic,
by [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]
and [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]; in
branch (C0) the heads of the graded Specht modules are the normalized simples
([[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)).

actual_incoming_interface_paragraphs:
The characteristic-zero theorems of this page
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]])
compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis
coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization
[[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]]
reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix
and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally
nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity
adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero
canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number
problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the
boundary recorded in
[[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]]
and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark
records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.

The two cited characteristic-zero theorems determine exactly the graded
decomposition numbers in branch (C0), where the transition polynomials
$d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$ are the global-basis coefficients. The
positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients
$a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, the
diagonal $1$ and the dominance support recorded in
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]; consequently
the "same" global-basis coefficients are not by themselves the answer in branch
(CP). The source's announced specialization of the adjustment matrix to the
matrix of James concerns the degenerate parameter and lies outside this page's
nondegenerate regime, as recorded in the batch coverage. No general
positive-characteristic formula is claimed, and this remark is not consumed to
prove any replacement statement. The boundary it states is the same one
recorded in the two unsolved-decomposition-number remarks cited in the
statement.

actual_incoming_interface_paragraphs:
In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ and every partition $\mu$ of content $\alpha$, the
graded decomposition polynomial factors as
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=\sum_{\nu\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\,d_{\nu,\mu}(q),$$
where $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ are the adjustment polynomials of
[[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]] and
$d_{\nu,\mu}$ the characteristic-independent global-basis transition polynomial
of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[J(\nu)]=[D(\nu)]+\sum_{\lambda\lhd\nu}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$. In
particular the characteristic-$p$ decomposition matrix is the product of the
dominance-unitriangular adjustment matrix and the (characteristic-independent)
matrix of global-basis coefficients, and no claim is made that the adjustment
matrix is the identity. Choice is inherited only through the transported
global-basis suppliers.

[F2] The reduced modules satisfy
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([J(\nu)])=D_\nu$ over the positive-characteristic
field, and the labels agree with the cellular heads in this branch
([[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]],
[[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]).

[F3] The adjustment polynomials are defined by
$[J(\nu)]=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$, with $a_{\nu,\nu}=1$
and $a_{\lambda,\nu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\nu$
([[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]); the graded
Grothendieck group has the shift-orbit basis of the normalized simples, so all
expansions are unique
([[cor-graded-specht-classes-form-a-basis-of-the-module-grothendieck-group]]).
